ai.description: This file implements the logic for the BasicTaker and Taker classes, which are central to the offer crossing and order matching mechanism in the XRPL decentralized exchange. The BasicTaker class manages the state and calculations for a taker (the party consuming offers), including tracking remaining amounts, determining if the taker is done or unfunded, and computing the flow of funds for different types of asset exchanges (XRP to IOU, IOU to XRP, IOU to IOU). It handles clamping flows based on available funds and offer limits, and logs the flow details for debugging. The Taker class extends BasicTaker by integrating with the ledger view, handling actual fund transfers (XRP and IOU), consuming offers, and updating ledger state. It supports both direct and bridged crossings (multi-leg trades), ensures proper fund checks, and manages the application of transfer rates and fees. The file includes robust assertions and error handling to maintain ledger integrity during complex offer crossings.

This file defines the base_uint template class, which represents fixed-size unsigned integers of arbitrary bit length (multiples of 32, at least 64 bits). It provides storage, construction, assignment, and arithmetic/bitwise operations for these integers, as well as parsing from hex strings and conversion to strings. The class is used to implement types like uint128, uint160, uint192, and uint256. The file also includes utility templates for checking if a container is contiguous, and provides comparison, hashing, and stream output operators for base_uint types. The design ensures no padding bytes and supports endian conversions for portability. The file is part of the Ripple/XRPL codebase and is used for cryptographic and protocol identifiers.

This file implements the core logic for handling IOU (I Owe You) amounts in the Ripple (XRPL) protocol. It provides functions and constants for representing, normalizing, and manipulating IOU amounts with high precision, using a mantissa and exponent format. The code includes mechanisms to switch between different number handling strategies, normalization routines to ensure values stay within valid ranges, and arithmetic operations such as addition and ratio multiplication (with rounding options). The mulRatio function uses high-precision arithmetic to safely multiply and divide IOU amounts, handling edge cases like overflow, underflow, and rounding. The file also provides utility functions for string conversion and internal state management. Overall, it ensures accurate and robust handling of non-native currency values in the XRPL system.

ai.description: This file defines the Logic class in the ripple::Resource namespace, which manages resource consumption and rate limiting for network endpoints in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. The Logic class tracks inbound, outbound, unlimited (admin), and inactive consumers using hash maps and intrusive lists, and provides thread-safe methods to create, update, and remove consumer entries. It supports charging fees, issuing warnings, disconnecting over-limit consumers, and exporting/importing consumer state for gossip-based sharing between servers. The class also provides JSON and property stream reporting of consumer states, and periodic cleanup of expired entries. The design ensures fair resource usage, prevents abuse, and supports administrative overrides.

This header file defines the PerfLogImp class, an implementation of the PerfLog interface for performance logging in the Ripple (XRPL) server. PerfLogImp tracks and logs performance metrics for RPC calls and job queue operations, including counts and durations for started, finished, and errored RPCs, as well as queued and running jobs. It uses thread-safe data structures (the Locked template) to manage counters and supports JSON reporting of current and cumulative statistics. The class manages its own logging thread, handles log file rotation, and provides methods to start, stop, and resize job tracking. The Counters struct organizes metrics for RPCs and jobs, and PerfLogImp integrates with the application and logging infrastructure, supporting asynchronous operation and safe shutdown.

This file implements the core of the performance logging system for the Rippled server. It defines the PerfLogImp class and its nested Counters class, which together track and log performance metrics for RPC methods and job queue activities. The Counters class maintains statistics such as started, finished, errored counts, and durations for both RPC calls and job types, and can serialize these statistics to JSON. PerfLogImp manages the lifecycle of the performance log, including opening/rotating the log file, periodically writing performance reports, and tracking the start and end of RPCs and jobs. It uses thread synchronization to ensure safe concurrent updates. The file also provides setup and factory functions for configuring and instantiating the performance logger. Overall, this code is responsible for collecting, aggregating, and persisting detailed operational metrics to help monitor and analyze the server's performance.

This file implements the logging system for the Ripple (XRPL) codebase. It defines the Logs class, which manages log sinks (destinations for log messages), log files, and log severity thresholds. This file implements the LedgerHistory class, which manages the caching, retrieval, and validation of ledgers in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. This file implements the core logic for the RCLConsensus class, which manages the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It defines the RCLConsensus and its nested Adaptor class, which acts as an interface between the consensus engine and the rest of the application. The Adaptor handles acquiring ledgers and transaction sets, sharing proposals and transactions with peers, proposing new ledgers, managing open transactions, and tracking consensus state. It also manages the process of closing and accepting ledgers, including building new ledgers, applying transactions, handling disputes, and validating ledgers. Overall, this file is central to the operation of distributed consensus in the XRPL node software, coordinating ledger agreement, transaction application, and network communication during consensus rounds.

The file does not define any classes, but contains three main functions: textTime (for formatting time durations), getCountsJson (for collecting and formatting statistics), and doGetCounts (the RPC handler).

The class manages the context of the RPC call, accesses ledger data, and formats the result as JSON. It provides methods to check the request and to write the result, including details from the requested ledger or, if unavailable, from the closed and open ledgers. The class specifies API version constraints and user role requirements, and uses several internal members to store context, ledger views, transaction queues, and result data.

This file implements the DatabaseRotatingImp class, which manages a rotating database backend system for the Ripple NodeStore. The class maintains two backends: a writable backend for current data and an archive backend for older data. It provides thread-safe operations for rotating (swapping) the backends, storing and fetching node objects, importing data from another database, synchronizing, and iterating over all stored objects. The rotate function swaps the writable backend with a new one, moves the old writable to archive, and deletes the previous archive. Fetch operations first try the writable backend, then the archive, and can optionally duplicate found objects back to the writable backend. The class uses mutex locks to ensure thread safety for all backend operations.

It manages resource usage, tracks balances, and enforces limits. The class provides constructors, copy/move semantics, and a destructor to handle resource acquisition and release. Key methods include checking if the consumer is unlimited, charging for resource usage, warning or disconnecting consumers, retrieving the current balance, and converting the consumer to a string representation. The class ensures proper resource management through assertions and by delegating actions to the Logic and Entry classes. An operator<< overload is provided for outputting the consumer's string representation.

The Sink class is an abstract base for log output destinations, supporting threshold filtering and optional console output. Journal provides Stream and ScopedStream classes for composing and emitting log messages in a stream-like fashion, with RAII semantics for message finalization. The file also defines logstream types for integrating with standard C++ stream APIs. The design enforces strict construction and assignment rules for safety and clarity, and provides static assertions to ensure correct usage.

The Logs class supports thread-safe logging, log file rotation, and dynamic adjustment of log thresholds. It includes nested classes: Sink (for writing logs to specific partitions) and File (for managing log file operations). This file implements the doLogLevel function, which handles the 'log_level' RPC command in the XRPL server. The function allows querying and setting the logging severity level for the application. If no severity is specified in the request, it returns the current log levels for all partitions. If a severity is provided, it sets the global or partition-specific log level accordingly. The function validates input parameters and returns appropriate error codes for invalid input.

This file defines the Logic class in the ripple::Resource namespace, which manages resource consumption and rate limiting for network endpoints in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. The Logic class tracks inbound, outbound, unlimited (admin), and inactive consumers using hash maps and intrusive lists, and provides thread-safe methods to create, update, and remove consumer entries. It supports charging fees, issuing warnings, disconnecting over-limit consumers, and exporting/importing consumer state for gossip-based sharing between servers. The class also provides JSON and property stream reporting of consumer states, and periodic cleanup of expired entries. The design ensures fair resource usage, prevents abuse, and supports administrative overrides.

This file implements the core network operations logic for the XRPL server (rippled). It handles state transitions (disconnected, connected, syncing, tracking, full), processes incoming and outgoing transactions, manages transaction batches, and coordinates consensus rounds. The class also provides mechanisms for clients to subscribe/unsubscribe to server events and account-specific updates, including historical transaction streaming. It tracks server fee metrics, publishes server and consensus status, and manages resource usage. The implementation includes detailed state accounting for monitoring and reporting, and supports both standalone and networked operation modes. The file also contains logic for handling book offers, peer status, and validator list management, ensuring the server stays in sync with the network and provides up-to-date information to clients.

It provides a highly generic, template-based Consensus class that manages the state and progression of consensus rounds among network peers. The consensus process involves collecting proposals from peers, tracking their positions, managing disputes over transactions, and determining when consensus has been reached or failed. The class handles transitions between different consensus phases (open, establish, accepted), manages timing and round progression, and provides mechanisms for pausing, simulating, and forcibly accepting consensus. The file includes utility functions for determining when to close a ledger, checking for consensus, and serializing the consensus state to JSON for monitoring or debugging. The class maintains two main caches: one for ledgers by hash and another for consensus-validated ledgers by index. It includes detailed logging and comparison functions to analyze and report differences between ledgers, especially in cases of mismatches during consensus. Overall, LedgerHistory is central to ensuring ledger consistency and diagnosing consensus issues in the XRPL server.

It defines methods for serializing, deserializing, comparing, and manipulating sets of payment paths (STPathSet), which are sequences of path elements (STPathElement) representing possible routes for payments through accounts, currencies, and issuers. The code includes functions for hashing path elements, constructing path sets from serialized data, copying and moving path sets, adding new paths while avoiding duplicates, checking for equivalence and default state, and converting paths and path sets to JSON. It also provides serialization support for writing path sets to binary form. The implementation ensures data integrity and proper error handling when parsing or manipulating path data.

The RCLConsensus class uses an internal Adaptor class to interface with application components such as the ledger master, local transactions, inbound transactions, and validator keys. The Adaptor encapsulates consensus parameters, state, and methods for interacting with the consensus algorithm, including handling proposals, mode changes, and ledger building. The file also defines a RclConsensusLogger class for logging consensus events. The design is modular, supporting extensibility and integration with other XRPL components, and provides thread safety via mutexes. The file includes interfaces for starting consensus rounds, processing timer events, handling peer proposals, and simulating consensus, as well as methods for retrieving consensus state and parameters.

This file implements components of a logging (journal) utility for the beast library in the XRPL codebase. This file defines a large set of constant JSON field names used throughout the Ripple (XRPL) protocol codebase. It uses a macro (JSS) to declare each field as a constexpr Json::StaticString, ensuring efficient and consistent use of JSON keys in the code. The file includes field names for accounts, transactions, ledgers, network status, and more, covering nearly all aspects of XRPL's JSON-based API and internal data structures. It also includes macros to automatically generate field names from included transaction and ledger entry macro files, ensuring extensibility and maintainability. No classes or functions are defined; the file is purely for JSON field name declarations.

void PerfLogImp::jobQueue(JobType const type) { auto counter = counters_.jq_.find(type); if (counter == counters_.jq_.end()) { UNREACHABLE( "ripple::perf::PerfLogImp::jobQueue : valid job type input"); return; } std::lock_guard lock(counter->second.mutex); ++counter->second.value.queued; }

void PerfLogImp::jobStart( JobType const type, microseconds dur, steady_time_point startTime, int instance) { auto counter = counters_.jq_.find(type); if (counter == counters_.jq_.end()) { UNREACHABLE( "ripple::perf::PerfLogImp::jobStart : valid job type input"); return; } { std::lock_guard lock(counter->second.mutex); ++counter->second.value.started; counter->second.value.queuedDuration += dur; } std::lock_guard lock(counters_.jobsMutex_); if (instance >= 0 && instance < counters_.jobs_.size()) counters_.jobs_[instance] = {type, startTime}; }

It handles node fetching (from cache, database, or sync filters), copy-on-write semantics for efficient memory usage, and supports snapshotting and flushing of the tree. The code ensures data integrity through assertions and error handling, and provides mechanisms for serializing, canonicalizing, and dumping the map's contents. The SHAMap supports both mutable and immutable states, and is designed for high performance and consistency in distributed ledger operations.

This file implements the InboundLedger class, which manages the acquisition and assembly of ledgers from the network in the XRPL (Ripple) node software. The class coordinates fetching ledger data (header, state, and transactions) from peers, handles timeouts and retries, and ensures data integrity. It interacts with local storage to check for already available data, requests missing pieces from peers, and processes incoming data. The class maintains state about which parts of the ledger have been acquired, manages peer selection and request strategies, and finalizes the ledger once all required data is obtained. It also provides JSON status reporting and handles concurrency and error conditions robustly. The file includes logic for filtering duplicate node requests, managing peer data quality, and integrating with the job queue for asynchronous processing. The PeerDataCounts struct is used internally to track and sample peers based on the usefulness of their responses.

This file defines the OpenLedger class, which manages the current open ledger in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. It provides thread-safe access and modification to the open ledger, allowing transactions to be applied, retried, or rejected according to specific rules and flags. The class uses mutexes for concurrency control and maintains a shared pointer to the current OpenView. Key methods include checking if the ledger is empty, accessing the current view, modifying the ledger with a user-provided function, and accepting new transactions with retry logic. The file also includes utility functions for debugging transaction and ledger states. The OpenLedger class is non-copyable and must be constructed with a ledger, cache, and logging journal. The apply method implements the logic for applying transactions, handling retries, and ensuring consistency. The file is part of the core ledger management infrastructure in the XRPL server.

This file defines a flexible logging (journal) utility for the Beast library, used in the XRPL codebase. It introduces a Journal class that manages log message output at various severity levels (trace, debug, info, warning, error, fatal, etc.) via a pluggable Sink interface. The Sink class is an abstract base for log output destinations, supporting threshold filtering and optional console output. Journal provides Stream and ScopedStream classes for composing and emitting log messages in a stream-like fashion, with RAII semantics for message finalization. The file also defines logstream types for integrating with standard C++ stream APIs. The design enforces strict construction and assignment rules for safety and clarity, and provides static assertions to ensure correct usage.

# NodeStore

## Introduction

A `NodeObject` is a simple object that the Ledger uses to store entries. It is comprised of a type, a hash and a blob. It can be uniquely identified by the hash, which is a 256 bit hash of the blob. The blob is a variable length block of serialized data. The type identifies what the blob contains. The fields are as follows:

`mType`

An enumeration that determines what the blob holds. There are four different types of objects stored.

**ledger**

A ledger header.

**transaction**

A signed transaction.

**account node**

A node in a ledger's account state tree.

**transaction node**

A node in a ledger's transaction tree.

`mHash`

A 256-bit hash of the blob.

It defines the Logs class, which manages log sinks (destinations for log messages), log files, and log severity thresholds. The system supports writing log messages to files and optionally to the console, with thread safety via mutexes. Log messages are formatted with timestamps, severity levels, and partition names, and sensitive information (like seeds and passphrases) is scrubbed from output. The file also provides utilities for rotating log files, converting between string and enum representations of log severities, and managing debug log sinks. The DebugSink class allows dynamic replacement and retrieval of a debug log sink, supporting thread-safe operations. Overall, the file provides a flexible, partitioned, and severity-aware logging infrastructure for the application.

This file implements the InboundLedgersImp class, which manages the acquisition and tracking of inbound ledgers in the Ripple (XRPL) server. It handles requests to acquire ledgers from the network, manages ongoing acquisitions, tracks failures, and processes incoming ledger data from peers. The class provides methods to acquire ledgers synchronously and asynchronously, check for failures, process stale data, clear caches, and report status information. It uses mutexes for thread safety and maintains internal maps for active acquisitions and recent failures. The file also includes a factory function to create instances of InboundLedgersImp. The overall design ensures efficient and robust management of ledger data needed for consensus and network operations.

ai.description: This file defines the JobTypes class, which manages and provides information about different job types used in the Ripple (XRPL) core system. Each job type is associated with a name, concurrency limit, average latency, and peak latency, encapsulated in JobTypeInfo objects. The JobTypes class maintains a map of all job types and their corresponding information, provides singleton access via the instance() method, and offers methods to retrieve job type names, information, and iterators for traversal. The class ensures that each job type is unique and includes a default 'invalid' job type for error handling. The job types cover a wide range of system tasks, including client commands, ledger operations, transaction processing, network operations, and administrative tasks.

This file implements the configuration logic for the XRPL (Ripple) server. It provides platform-specific functions to determine system memory, parses INI-style configuration files, and manages configuration sections and values. The core class, Config, handles loading and interpreting configuration files, setting up directories, and initializing various server parameters such as node size, database paths, peer limits, network settings, and feature flags. The file includes validation and error handling for configuration values, supports environment variable overrides, and manages validator file loading and parsing. It also provides utility functions for retrieving configuration values, setting up fee voting parameters, and ensuring proper server setup based on the configuration. The design ensures robust, flexible, and platform-independent configuration management for the XRPL server.

This file implements various low-level database operations for the XRPL (Ripple) ledger and transaction relational database backend. It provides functions to manage, query, and maintain ledger and transaction data in SQLite databases. Key functionalities include: mapping table types to strings, creating and configuring ledger and transaction databases, retrieving minimum and maximum ledger sequences, deleting ledger data by sequence, counting rows, saving validated ledgers (with integrity checks and serialization), retrieving ledger info by index or hash, fetching transaction history, and paginated account transaction queries. The file also includes logic for checking available database and disk space, and for handling transaction deserialization errors. The code is tightly integrated with the application's logging, configuration, and ledger management subsystems, and makes extensive use of the SOCI C++ database library for SQL operations.

This file implements the STLedgerEntry class, which represents a ledger entry in the XRP Ledger. The class provides constructors for creating ledger entries from a Keylet, a serialized iterator, or an existing STObject. It manages the type and key of the ledger entry, applies the correct template based on the entry type, and provides methods for serialization, copying, moving, and generating textual and JSON representations of the entry. The class also includes logic for handling threaded ledger entries, which track previous transaction IDs and ledger sequences, and determines if an entry type supports threading based on protocol rules. Error handling is present for unknown or invalid ledger entry types.

This file implements various low-level database operations for the XRPL (Ripple) ledger and transaction relational database backend. It provides functions to manage, query, and maintain ledger and transaction data in SQLite databases. Key functionalities include: mapping table types to strings, creating and configuring ledger and transaction databases, retrieving minimum and maximum ledger sequences, deleting ledger data by sequence, counting rows, saving validated ledgers (with integrity checks and serialization), retrieving ledger info by index or hash, fetching transaction history, and paginated account transaction queries. The file also includes logic for checking available database and disk space, and for handling transaction deserialization errors. The code is tightly integrated with the application's logging, configuration, and ledger management subsystems, and makes extensive use of the SOCI C++ database library for SQL operations.

This file implements the LedgerHistory class, which manages the caching, retrieval, and validation of ledgers in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. It provides mechanisms to insert ledgers into caches, retrieve them by hash or sequence number, and handle mismatches between built and validated ledgers. The class maintains two main caches: one for ledgers by hash and another for consensus-validated ledgers by index. It includes detailed logging and comparison functions to analyze and report differences between ledgers, especially in cases of mismatches during consensus. The file also provides utility functions for cache maintenance, such as clearing old entries and fixing index-to-hash mappings. Overall, LedgerHistory is central to ensuring ledger consistency and diagnosing consensus issues in the XRPL server.

This file implements the PeerImp class, which represents a peer connection in the XRPL (Ripple) overlay network. PeerImp manages the lifecycle and communication of a peer, including connection setup, message sending and receiving, protocol negotiation, resource usage tracking, and feature support. It handles various protocol messages (transactions, validations, proposals, ledger data, etc.), manages transaction and ledger queues, enforces resource limits, and supports features like transaction reduce-relay, ledger replay, and squelching. The class also tracks peer metrics (latency, bytes sent/received), manages peer status and tracking (converged/diverged), and interacts with other network components such as the job queue, ledger master, validators, and resource manager. The file includes logic for relaying messages, handling protocol errors, charging peers for resource usage, and maintaining peer state for network health and synchronization.

This file implements the SHAMapStoreImp class, which manages the storage, rotation, and deletion of SHAMap (state tree) data in the XRPL node database. It handles online deletion of old ledger data, manages backend databases (including rotating between writable and archive backends), and ensures data integrity during ledger rotations. The class coordinates with other components such as the ledger master, transaction master, and network operations to determine when it is safe to delete or rotate data. It also manages cache freshness and database paths, and provides mechanisms for safe shutdown and health monitoring. The SHAMapStoreImp::SavedStateDB nested class manages persistent state related to deletion and rotation. The file includes logic for initializing the store, handling ledger closures, rotating databases, clearing old data from SQL tables, and maintaining minimum online ledger requirements. Overall, it is a core component for efficient and safe ledger data lifecycle management in the XRPL server.

This file implements the LedgerCleaner component for the XRPL (Ripple) server. The main class, LedgerCleanerImp, manages a background thread that cleans and repairs ledger data within a specified range. It can check for missing or inconsistent ledger nodes and transactions, and attempts to fix them by reacquiring or saving ledgers as needed. The class supports starting and stopping the cleaning process, configuring the cleaning range and options via JSON parameters, and reporting its status. The cleaning process is careful to avoid running during high server load and tracks failures, retrying as necessary. The file also provides a factory function to create instances of the LedgerCleaner.

This header file defines the PerfLogImp class, an implementation of the PerfLog interface for performance logging in the Ripple (XRPL) server. PerfLogImp tracks and logs performance metrics for RPC calls and job queue operations, including counts and durations for started, finished, and errored RPCs, as well as queued and running jobs. It uses thread-safe data structures (the Locked template) to manage counters and supports JSON reporting of current and cumulative statistics. The class manages its own logging thread, handles log file rotation, and provides methods to start, stop, and resize job tracking. The Counters struct organizes metrics for RPCs and jobs, and PerfLogImp integrates with the application and logging infrastructure, supporting asynchronous operation and safe shutdown.

This file implements the LedgerReplayer class, which manages the process of replaying a sequence of ledgers in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) system. The class coordinates tasks for replaying ledgers, acquiring skip lists, and creating ledger deltas. It ensures that replay tasks are not duplicated or merged when possible, manages resource limits, and handles concurrency with mutex locks. The main methods include starting a replay task (replay), creating deltas between ledgers (createDeltas), handling received skip list and delta data (gotSkipList, gotReplayDelta), cleaning up finished or expired tasks and resources (sweep), and stopping all ongoing operations (stop). The class uses shared and weak pointers to manage the lifecycle of replay tasks, skip lists, and deltas, and logs significant events for debugging and monitoring.

This file implements the core network operations logic for the XRPL server (rippled). The main class, NetworkOPsImp, manages the server's operating mode, transaction processing (both synchronous and asynchronous), consensus participation, ledger publication, and subscription management for various real-time data streams (such as ledgers, transactions, validations, and account history). It handles state transitions (disconnected, connected, syncing, tracking, full), processes incoming and outgoing transactions, manages transaction batches, and coordinates consensus rounds. The class also provides mechanisms for clients to subscribe/unsubscribe to server events and account-specific updates, including historical transaction streaming. It tracks server fee metrics, publishes server and consensus status, and manages resource usage. The implementation includes detailed state accounting for monitoring and reporting, and supports both standalone and networked operation modes. The file also contains logic for handling book offers, peer status, and validator list management, ensuring the server stays in sync with the network and provides up-to-date information to clients.

This header file defines a set of invariant check classes used in the Ripple (XRPL) transaction processing engine. Each class represents a specific invariant that must be maintained during transaction application, such as ensuring no XRP is created, account roots are not improperly deleted, ledger entry types match, no bad offers or zero escrows are created, and various checks for NFTs, AMMs, and permissioned domains/DEXs. Each invariant checker provides visitEntry and finalize methods to inspect ledger changes and validate invariants after transaction execution. The file also defines a tuple type, InvariantChecks, aggregating all these checkers, and a function to instantiate them. These invariants help ensure ledger integrity and prevent protocol violations during transaction processing.

This file defines the interface for the Application class in the Ripple (XRPL) server. The Application class acts as the central coordinator for the server, providing access to core components such as configuration, logging, networking, ledger management, validation, resource management, and various caches. It is an abstract class with numerous pure virtual methods for starting, running, and stopping the application, as well as for accessing and managing subsystems like the job queue, overlay network, ledger master, transaction queue, validators, and databases. The file also declares a factory function for creating an Application instance and includes forward declarations for many related classes used throughout the server. The Application class inherits from beast::PropertyStream::Source, enabling property streaming for diagnostics or monitoring.
